Kept the canonical seating and media clusters, trimmed seating to a sofa-plus-table core, and added a minimal lighting support cluster because the brief explicitly asks for ample lighting and the room has daylight plus media use.
Did not add entry or pet support because the brief does not require them and the room should stay open and easy to move through.
20m2 living room with strong center-openness and media-wall priority supports core seating and TV console as mandatory.
Support clusters remain useful but should be filtered more aggressively than core; small support items may survive only when surplus is comfortable.
Lighting is favored because daylight is present yet media use is explicit; bookshelf/storage are optional and should drop before circulation-sensitive items.
Preserve center openness and entry circulation.
Media wall is the primary focal constraint; seating should face it.
Daylight is beneficial for seating but should not block the window region.
Storage is optional and must stay peripheral to circulation.
Request contract LLM mode is the default runtime path; deterministic validation remains active.
SemanticLayoutPlanner used the room profile registry as the canonical rule source.
Planner output is cluster/bundle/zone level only; pose is left to downstream composer and solver.
Style policy compiled before layout planning; downstream geometry treats it as bias, not a hard override.
Request contract attached before tier count so explicit functional objects are protected from silent pruning.
Cluster main_seating: relaxed wall attachment for core social cluster to allow floating exploration.
Tier Count used deterministic utility, capacity, and bundle-preserving rules, plus Forge semantic tier-count hints when available.
Tier Count itself did not run an additional LLM call.
Output is synchronized for the object-level anchor-first solver handoff.
Merged into solver-ready object program for object-level anchor-first placement.
Living room correction preserved social clarity and focal logic.
